The provider guide you mentioned is `/home/simon/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v25.4.0/installation/lib/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent/docs/providers.md`.

It explains that Pi can get credentials via subscriptions (OAuth, e.g., Google Gemini/Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Claude, Copilot, etc.), API keys, or an `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` auth file. For API keys it expects the usual provider-specific env vars (Anthropic: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, OpenAI: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, Gemini: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, Mistral: `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, and so on—see the table in the doc). The auth file can embed literal keys, pull from env vars, or run a shell command to fetch them, and it takes precedence over environment variables. If you’d rather not set env vars, populate that file instead (Pi creates it with `0600` permissions). The doc also covers cloud providers (Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex) and custom extensions.

Let me know if you want help setting any of these up or converting an existing key to the auth file format.
